subject: river bridge
title: What If a Bridge Built From Both Banks Didn't Meet? One Missed by 54 cm

scenes.text: What if a bridge built from both banks didn't meet? One missed by 54 centimetres.
The Rhine, 2003. Germany builds from one bank, Switzerland from the other, toward the same point in mid-air.
Both countries measure height above sea level. But Germany's sea is the North Sea, and Switzerland's is the Mediterranean. Their zeros sit 27 centimetres apart.
The engineers knew that, and corrected for it. Somewhere in the sums, the correction went in the wrong direction.
So instead of cancelling the gap, it doubled it. In December 2003 the German side stood 54 centimetres higher than the Swiss side.
The German end was lowered, the insurance paid, and the bridge opened on schedule a year later. The two seas still disagree.

description:
What if a bridge built from both banks didn't meet in the middle? At Laufenburg on the Rhine, one missed by 54 centimetres.
Germany and Switzerland each built half of a new bridge between the twin towns of Laufenburg. German heights are referenced to the North Sea and Swiss heights to the Mediterranean, a 27 centimetre difference. It was known and corrected for, but the correction was applied the wrong way and the offset doubled to 54 centimetres, discovered in December 2003. The German side was lowered and the bridge opened in December 2004.
